results.description: Personal data of EU persons may only be stored in the EU, the EEA, or an adequate country.

questions.data_residency: Where is personal data stored in production?

results.why: Personal data of EU persons is hosted in Amazon RDS us-east-1 (United States). Accepted destinations are EU, EEA, or a country with an adequacy decision.

actions: Migrate the production datastore that holds personal data to an EU or EEA region (for example eu-north-1 / Finland).
Stop processing EU personal data in this system until the transfer tool is in place.
steps: Inventory which tables and object stores contain names, emails, or other personal data.
Choose an approved EU/EEA region and plan a cutover (snapshot, restore, DNS, secrets).
Update hosting documentation so the recorded residency is EU, EEA, or adequacy.
Re-run the compliance health check after production traffic is in the new region.

results.description: Each processing activity must have a recorded lawful basis under Article 6.

questions.lawful_basis: What is the lawful basis for processing personal data?

results.why: The project recorded legitimate interest for CRM analytics, which is an accepted lawful basis.

actions: No change required for this check.

results.description: An Article 28 DPA must be signed when a processor handles personal data; otherwise not_applicable.

questions.dpa_signed: Is a data processing agreement signed with every processor?

results.why: A data processing agreement is on file with the current cloud processor, so this statement passes.

actions: No change required for this check.

results.description: Personal data must not be kept longer than a documented, finite retention period.

questions.retention_policy: Is a finite retention period defined and enforced?

results.why: Event logs and CRM extracts are kept indefinitely. GDPR storage limitation requires a defined, enforced retention period.

actions: Publish a retention schedule (for example 24 months for analytics events, 12 months for marketing extracts).
Turn on automated deletion or anonymisation when the period expires.
steps: Agree retention periods with the DPO for each personal-data store.
Implement TTL, lifecycle rules, or a scheduled wipe job.
Document the schedule in the record of processing and set retention_policy to defined.
Re-run the health check.

results.description: This processing activity must be listed in the organisation’s record of processing activities.

questions.ropa_recorded: Is this processing listed in the organisation RoPA?

results.why: Whether GrowthBoard is listed in the organisation’s record of processing activities was not answered, so this check cannot pass or fail yet.

actions: Confirm with the DPO whether GrowthBoard is already in the RoPA.
If it is missing, file the processing activity before the next health check.
steps: Email the Data Protection Officer with the product name, data categories, and processors.
Record ropa_recorded as yes once the entry exists, or leave it empty only while the DPO investigates.
Re-run the health check after the RoPA row is confirmed.

results.description: Each production AI system must record an AI Act risk class that is not prohibited.

questions.ai_risk_class: What is the AI Act risk class of production AI in this project?

results.why: GrowthBoard’s lead-scoring model is recorded as high-risk. This closed check only accepts limited, minimal, or not_applicable until governance extends the enum.

actions: Confirm the risk class with the AI Act officer — marketing scoring may be limited-risk if it does not decide access to education or employment.
If the use is high-risk, add the missing high_risk value to accepted only after a human review of Annex III.
steps: Describe what the model decides (ranking vs automated exclusion).
Ask the AI Act officer whether Annex III applies.
Either stop automated ranking, add a named reviewer, or update the closed schema after sign-off.
Re-run the health check.

results.description: High-risk AI that affects people must have a named human reviewer.

questions.human_oversight: Is a named human reviewer in the loop for AI decisions that affect people?

results.why: Lead scoring ranks CRM contacts with no named reviewer who can override the score.

actions: Name a reviewer who must approve or can override scores before they change outreach.
Disable automated ranking until oversight is in place.
steps: Assign a named role (for example the campaign owner).
Document the override path in the model card.
Set human_oversight to yes and re-run the health check.

results.description: High-impact AI outputs must be logged for at least 90 days.

questions.ai_logging: Are high-impact AI outputs logged for at least 90 days?

results.why: Lead-score outputs are retained in the analytics warehouse for more than 90 days.

actions: No change required for this check.

results.description: Production AI features must publish a model card (purpose, family, limitations).

questions.model_card: Is a model card published for production AI features?

results.why: The lead-scoring model is in production without a published model card.

actions: Publish a short model card: purpose, model family, and known limitations.
Link it from the project README.
steps: Draft purpose (CRM ranking), family, and limitations (bias, no exclusion decisions).
Store the card next to the policy review.
Set model_card to yes and re-run the health check.
